coldOpen: The Bluetooth logo is a Viking king's initials.
centralQuestion: Why is the Bluetooth logo that angular symbol, and where did the name come from?

sources.name: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: King Harald Bluetooth Gormsson was known for uniting Denmark and Norway in 958.
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: Harald's nickname came from a dead tooth of a dark blue-grey colour.
evidence.quote: His dead tooth, which was a dark blue/grey color, and earned him the nickname Bluetooth
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: In 1996 Intel, Ericsson and Nokia met to plan the standardization of a short-range radio technology.
evidence.quote: In 1996, three industry leaders, Intel, Ericsson, and Nokia, met to plan the standardization of this short-range radio technology
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: At that meeting Jim Kardach of Intel suggested Bluetooth as a temporary code name.
evidence.quote: Jim Kardach from Intel suggested Bluetooth as a temporary code name
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: Kardach compared Harald uniting Scandinavia with uniting the PC and cellular industries through a short-range wireless link.
evidence.quote: was famous for uniting Scandinavia just as we intended to unite the PC and cellular industries with a short-range wireless link
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: Bluetooth was intended only as a placeholder name.
evidence.quote: Bluetooth was only intended as a placeholder until marketing could come up with something really cool
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: The planned replacement names were RadioWire or PAN (Personal Area Networking).
evidence.quote: Bluetooth was to be replaced with either RadioWire or PAN (Personal Area Networking)
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: PAN already had tens of thousands of hits on the internet.
evidence.quote: PAN was the front runner, but an exhaustive search discovered it already had tens of thousands of hits throughout the internet
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: A full trademark search on RadioWire could not be completed in time for launch.
evidence.quote: A full trademark search on RadioWire couldn't be completed in time for launch, making Bluetooth the only choice
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: The Bluetooth logo is a bind rune merging the Younger Futhark runes Hagall and Bjarkan, Harald's initials.
evidence.quote: The Bluetooth logo is a bind rune merging the Younger Futhark runes
evidence.source: Bluetooth SIG — Origin of the Name

evidence.claim: Kardach proposed the code name after seeing a picture of Harald Bluetooth's runestone in a history of the Vikings.
evidence.quote: Upon discovering a picture of the runestone of Harald Bluetooth in the book A History of the Vikings by Gwyn Jones
